claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC alloy with a dendritic microstructure.
The unmodified TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The unmodified TiVNbTa alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 1273 K.
Adding a small amount of Hf and applying a tailored heat treatment will produce a fine dispersion of Hf-oxide precipitates in TiVNbTa.
The resulting Hf-oxide precipitates will be thermally stable at 1273 K.
Oxide precipitation can strengthen a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Finely dispersed Hf-oxide precipitates will impede dislocation motion in the modified TiVNbTa alloy.
The Hf-oxide precipitates will inhibit grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
Hf addition can be associated with high elevated-temperature strength in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed modification will arrest high-temperature softening of TiVNbTa at 1273 K.
The modified alloy will reach or exceed approximately 500 MPa yield strength at 1273 K.
The modified alloy will retain adequate ductility under strains of roughly 30–40%.
The strengthening treatment will not compromise thermal conductivity.
The modified alloy will retain heat-transfer properties adequate for use as an intermediate layer between W and CuCrZr.

contradictions.description: The mechanism states that strengthening occurs without compromising thermal conductivity, whereas the uncertainty field explicitly says that a negative impact on thermal conductivity remains unresolved.
